answer.answer: The retained passages support that cryptocurrency can be property held on trust, but actual ownership depends on the relevant relationship, terms and consent. The 2023 conclusion excludes non-consenting customers from its general rejection of customer trusts under the 2018 terms. The 2025 disposition recognises pooled beneficial interests for non-consenting customers and distinguishes their position from ETD holders and Mr Samara. These conclusions do not establish a Product Provider’s ownership arrangements or fulfillment of paragraph 10 of 26EC22. Transfer requires an applicable legal proposition, materially comparable relationships and proven facts. Subsequent treatment and the conflicting scenario-seven wording remain unresolved.

claims.proposition: The 2023 conclusion recognises cryptocurrency as property capable of trust, while rejecting the claimed trust under the 2018 terms and preserving the non-consenting-customer exception.
claims.status: Supported by the retained conclusion; broader ratio and application not independently established.

support.quote: Except the Non-Consenting Customers, the 2018 T&C applied to, and governed the relationship between all the Customers (be it Group A, B or C customers) and Gatecoin
Cryptocurrency is “property” and is capable of being held on trust
There was certainty of subject matter and object. However, the terms of the 2018 T&C show that there was no certainty of intention to create a trust over the cryptocurrencies held by Gatecoin

claims.inference: The text distinguishes capacity to be trust property from creation of a trust in a particular relationship. It does not establish that all cryptocurrency holders have beneficial ownership.
missing_premises: The applicable customer terms and evidence of consent.
The actual relationship and facts supporting certainty of intention in the proposed application.

claims.proposition: Ownership and custody labels do not conclusively establish a proprietary interest or trustee relationship.
claims.status: Supported as quoted reasoning, with attribution preserved.

support.quote: The words used by the parties such as ‘trust’, ‘custody’, ‘belonging’, ‘ownership’, ‘title’, may be persuasive, but they are not conclusive in favour of the recognition of B’s proprietary interest in the property, if the terms of the agreement or relationship, viewed objectively, compel a different conclusion.

The identification of a relationship in which A is B’s agent or broker is not conclusive of a conclusion that A is, in relation to the property, B’s trustee, although it may be a pointer towards that conclusion.

claims.inference: This is a principle quoted from Re Lehman Brothers in the retained reasons. Its application requires objective assessment of the particular agreement and relationship, rather than reliance on labels or token possession alone.
missing_premises: Full reasoning establishing the principle’s role in the decision.
Terms and conduct of each relevant pair of parties.

claims.proposition: Non-consenting customers, ETD holders and Mr Samara have materially different positions; BlueFire account entries likewise do not alone determine ownership.
claims.status: Supported by retained passages, subject to their factual scope.

support.quote: Each NCC is a beneficial tenant-in-common in a pool of cryptocurrency and fiat currency.
ETD represents a cause of action by ETD Holder against Gatecoin for breach of trust.
Gatecoin does not hold the Subject Bitcoins or the Specified Account on trust for Mr Samara.
Mr Samara is only an unsecured creditor to the extent of his claim less the amount he already received through execution of the HCA Judgment.
The Currencies recorded in BlueFire’s accounts are assets of Gatecoin.

claims.inference: The 2025 disposition assigns distinct consequences to distinct relationships. A beneficial share in a pool is not an entitlement to identified coins; a breach-of-trust claim and an unsecured claim also require separate treatment.
missing_premises: Evidence identifying the relevant customer or claimant category.
The full reasons and conditions governing allocation, costs and remedies.

claims.proposition: Consent classification depends on evidence, and the scenario-seven tension remains open.

support.quote: The customers should be regarded as NCCs unless there is evidence to show that they have accessed or used the Platform to effect the transactions
The transactions described in the 7th scenario did not exist and the customers should not be regarded as NCC.

The 5th to 7th scenarios prima facie fall outside the definition of NCC but if the customers can prove that they gave the relevant instructions to Gatecoin before the Relevant Date or without using the Platform, they should be regarded as NCCs.

Transactions relating to limit order which a Customer claims was not executed immediately but only when the set price was reached, unless such Customer is able to prove that the order was placed before 6 March 2018.

Any Customer who claims to have transactions enumerated in paragraphs 1.2(b) shall notify the Liquidators and provide evidence to the Liquidators in support of such a claim within 21 days from the date hereof.

claims.inference: Paragraph 8 makes scenarios one to four presumptively non-consenting absent contrary evidence and scenarios five to six dependent on proof overcoming apparent platform use. Paragraph 95 extends that latter qualification to seven, although paragraph 8 rejects seven’s factual existence. The annexure supplies specific transaction and evidence provisions. These texts cannot safely be collapsed into a complete automatic consent classifier.
missing_premises: A justified reconciliation of paragraph 8, paragraph 95 and the annexure.
Customer-specific platform-access, instruction-date and transaction evidence.
Verification of the full reasons and operative directions.

claims.proposition: Transfer to a Product Provider requires separate authority, applicability, analogy and factual premises; neither ownership classification nor duty applicability establishes regulatory fulfillment.
claims.status: Source-grounded deduction and proposed application requirements; transfer not established.

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.
the ownership representation of the tokens (eg, legal and beneficial title of the tokens, ownership of / interests in the product)

claims.inference: Gatecoin may inform analysis of proprietary relationships, but the retained passages do not interpret 26EC22. Paragraph 10 assigns continuing responsibility despite outsourcing; it neither creates a trust nor supplies a complete fulfillment test. Applying Gatecoin therefore requires a reasoned legal analogy, not a shared reference to cryptocurrency or ownership records.
missing_premises: The precise proposition’s ratio, authority and subsequent treatment at the assessment date.
Applicability of the retained 26EC22 edition, relevant conditions and amendments, and the entity’s Product Provider role.
Material comparability of product rights, governing law, contracts, consent, custody and outsourcing relationships.
Evidence distinguishing ownership of the token from interests in the underlying product.
An applicable fulfillment standard and actual evidence of retained authority, supervisory conduct, operational soundness and proper ownership records throughout the relevant interval.

rival_readings: For scenario seven, paragraph 8 supports factual exclusion; paragraph 95 expressly includes it within a rebuttable classification covering scenarios five to seven. The retained annexure does not resolve that discrepancy. Neither wording is silently preferred.

A narrow use of Gatecoin confines its ownership conclusions to the proven exchange-customer relationships. A broader analogy may draw on objective assessment of terms and consent, but requires independently justified transfer to the Product Provider’s relationships.
unresolved: The 2025 passage records the 2023 conclusions, but does not establish complete subsequent treatment or current binding force. The candidate’s 'followed' label is not a complete citator result; hypothetical overruled controls are not evidence of actual overruling.
Only selected judgment passages are supplied. Candidate assertions of full-reasons checking do not establish that this assessment has checked the full reasons, disposition or rendered documents.
Both candidate case manifests use the same source hash, whereas the supplied source-file records give distinct hashes. The provenance discrepancy remains unexplained.
Scenario-seven reconciliation and a complete consent classifier remain unresolved.

No actual Product Provider facts, applicable discharge standard or legally justified source-to-rule transfer establish fulfillment. Parser, graph and serialization acceptance cannot supply those premises.
